SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

10. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

11. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

2. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

3. D — newton (N)

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

5. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

6. A — Glucose and oxygen

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

8. C — Producers

9. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

10. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

11. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Invertebrates; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Change of State; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Composition of Air; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
